extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). The 404 error handler passes request.path (attacker-controlled URL) into render_template_string via an f-string: render_template_string(f"{error}. Requested URL was {request.path}"). An attacker can request a path containing Jinja2 template syntax (e.g. /{{config}} or /{{''.__class__.__mro__[...].__subclasses__()}}) to execute arbitrary code or leak the SECRET_KEY, because an unmatched route triggers a 404 which renders the attacker-controlled path as a template.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: The Flask secret key is hardcoded as "super secret key" (app.secret_key = "super secret key"). This key signs and encrypts Flask session cookies. Because it is publicly known from the source code, an attacker can forge arbitrary session cookies, bypass authentication, and impersonate any user (including admins).

SQL Injection. In validate_token(), the user-supplied registration code (form.registration_code.data) is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string via an f-string: text(f"SELECT id, code FROM {RegistrationCode.__tablename__} WHERE code = '{code}'"). An attacker can break out of the string literal with a single quote and inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. ' UNION SELECT id, code FROM registration_code --) to extract data or manipulate query results. A parameterized query or ORM filter should be used instead.

SQL Injection. In the /search route, the search parameter from request.args.get('search') is concatenated directly into a raw SQL fragment via an f-string: text(f"text like '%{search_param}%'"). An attacker can inject e.g. %' OR 1=1 -- to break out of the LIKE clause and return all notes (including other users' private notes), or use UNION-based injection to extract arbitrary data from the database.

Insecure Deserialization leading to Remote Code Execution. The before_request hook deserializes the user-controlled 'preferences' cookie using pickle.loads(b64decode(preferences)) on every request, with no authentication required. pickle.loads can execute arbitrary code during deserialization. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload (e.g. using __reduce__), base64-encode it, set it as the 'preferences' cookie, and achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on the server.

Mass assignment / privilege escalation. The update_account route copies all form fields (including is_admin) directly onto current_user via current_user.__dict__.update(filtered_values) and then persists with session.merge(current_user). The AccountForm exposes an 'is_admin' BooleanField with no server-side authorization check. A non-admin user can craft a POST to /account with is_admin=y (the checkbox is only hidden in the UI for non-admins) to set is_admin=True and escalate to administrator privileges.

IDOR / Broken Access Control. The /accounts/<int:user_id>/notes route fetches ALL notes for the given user_id (session.query(Note).filter(Note.user_id == user_id)) including private notes, without verifying that user_id matches current_user.id. Any authenticated user can change user_id in the URL (e.g. /accounts/1/notes) to read other users' private notes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Missing authentication. The POST /account (update_account) route lacks the @login_required decorator, unlike the GET /account route which is protected. This allows unauthenticated users to submit the account update form and trigger processing of form data (including the mass-assignment of is_admin) without being authenticated. The route should be protected with @login_required.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The download() function calls urlopen(url) with no validation or restriction on the target host/scheme. The url originates from user input (form.url.data submitted to POST /account/image). An attacker can supply a URL pointing to internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ for cloud metadata, or internal network hosts) to read internal resources, and the response is base64-encoded and stored/displayed. urlopen also supports file:// which may allow reading local files.

IDOR / Broken Access Control. The delete_note route fetches a note by id (session.get(Note, note_id)) and deletes it without checking that the note belongs to current_user (the template only hides the delete button, but the server enforces nothing). Any authenticated user can delete any note belonging to any user by POSTing to /notes/<note_id>/delete with an arbitrary note_id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Hardcoded default credentials. The database is seeded with a normal user (user@evfa.com / password 'user') and an admin (admin@evfa.com / password 'admin'), plus a static, publicly-known registration code 'a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764' (line 9). These credentials exist in production after seeding, allowing an attacker to log in as admin (admin/admin) and a static code to register new accounts.

Sensitive information exposure via logging. The SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, which logs every SQL statement (including bound parameters such as emails, password hashes, and note contents) to stdout/logs. In production this can expose sensitive data and should be disabled.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Note text is rendered with the Jinja2 'safe' filter: {{ note.text | safe }}, which disables HTML escaping. Note content is user-controlled (created via CKEditor on POST /notes) and notes are shared across all users on the home feed (get_notes_for_user returns all public notes). An attacker can create a public note containing <script>...</script> to execute arbitrary JavaScript in every viewer's browser, enabling session theft and account takeover.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The render_table macro is called with safe_columns=['text'], which marks the note 'text' column as safe and renders it without HTML escaping. Note text is user-controlled (created via CKEditor). An attacker can inject malicious HTML/JavaScript into a note; when another user views personal notes (including via the IDOR at /accounts/<user_id>/notes), the script executes in their browser.
